title: Overlay VNI learning table saturation causes transient ARP/DNS ghosting and egress blackholes during scale events
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Multiple customers on Dedicated clusters reported intermittent cross-tenant ARP and DNS responses, followed by short periods of outbound blackholing after autoscaling events and VPC peering switchover. Surface: tenant A sees ARP replies that map to hosts in tenant B for a few seconds (ghost entries), and some flows briefly fail or route to the wrong gateway until the dataplane relearns. This has caused production errors (failed RPCs, 502/504 retries) for three high-usage Dedicated customers during scale-up and peering rotation windows.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision Dedicated cluster with two tenants that have non-overlapping VPCs but share overlay fabric (VNI per-tenant).
2) Drive synthetic workload on tenant A to create many ephemeral host attachments and high ARP churn (simulate scale-up).
3) Trigger node autoscale-out (add worker) and force VTEP learning updates, or simulate a peering switchover by flapping the peering gateway.
4) Observe overlay learning table (VTEP/VNI map) growth, map evictions, and transient ARP/DNS responses that match stale mappings.
5) Confirm some outbound flows are blackholed until the dataplane relearns correct VNI->MAC mappings or until control-plane reconciliation completes.
impact: medium to high depending on workload: failed end-user requests, increased retries, and possible exposure of private hostnames in DNS answers for short windows. Affected customers reported SLO breaches during peak scale events. Not actively used as an exploit but violates tenant isolation guarantees.
root_cause: The overlay VNI learning table (dataplane FIB) can grow rapidly during scale events. Our asynchronous learning GC and the accelerated offload path (kernel/eBPF) use a global eviction policy that can evict entries across VNIs. During concurrent peering or autoscale operations the control-plane briefly accepts and distributes stale mappings that are compatible with other VNIs, creating transient cross-tenant replies. Additionally, conntrack namespace invalidation lag allowed short-lived flows to be associated with stale mappings before cleanup.
mitigation: 1) Immediately deployed a cluster-level config to reduce max learning table size and increase per-VNI isolation on affected Dedicated clusters (hotfix rolled 2026-03-05). 2) Added temporary traffic shaping to limit ARP/probe storms during controlled autoscale windows. 3) Communication: notified impacted customers and opened support tickets with mitigation steps.
fix_description: Primary fix (PR #9876): switch from a global overlay FIB eviction policy to a per-VNI LRU buckets with hardened invalidation on peering or VNI reparent events. Ensure the dataplane map resize path is atomic and that control-plane replays include a tombstone sequence to prevent acceptance of stale mappings. Also patch conntrack namespace cleanup to run synchronously for affected namespaces during scale/peering operations. The fix includes unit + integration tests and eBPF map compatibility guards for older kernels.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR #9876 to stable branch and build runtime-1.22.1-dedicated-hotfix (artifact: runtime-1.22.1+ded-hotfix).
2) Install to staging Dedicated clusters and run full integration tests (48h soak).
3) Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated tenants with high ARP churn profiles for 24h. Monitor metrics and error budget impact.
4) Gradually increase to 25% then full fleet over 72 hours if no regressions observed.
5) Manual rollback plan: revert to runtime-1.22.0 disabled map resizing and restore previous eviction flags; clear eBPF maps on nodes as part of rollback to guarantee clean state.
test_plan: - Unit tests for per-VNI LRU logic and tombstone replay semantics.
- Integration scenario: synthetic scale-up + peering-flap test ensuring no cross-VNI map answers and 0 cross_tenant_arp_alerts.
- Chaos test: force kubelet/worker restart and ensure no long-lived stale entries; measure ARP miss latency and DNS answer correctness.
- Backwards-compat tests: nodes on older kernel versions should continue to operate; add graceful fallback to software path if eBPF resizing not available.
monitoring_and_alerting: Added new dashboards: Overlay->VNI Map Evictions, CrossTenantARPAlerts, ConntrackNamespaceCleanupLatency.
New alerts: cross_tenant_arp_alert_count > 1 in 5m (P0), overlay_map_eviction_rate > 100/s (P1), conntrack_namespace_cleanup_latency > 500ms (P1).
Post-rollout verification: monitor tenant isolation error rate and customer support reduction for 72h window.
